title: Systematic Analysis of Concept and Term “Green Logistics”
content: The term “Green logistics” appeared more than 20 years ago and still provokes debate among scientists and business representatives. The number of publications on green logistics is increasing by an average of 17–31% each year, confirming researchers' interest in implementing modern concepts related to environmental protection in logistics activities. Despite the large number of publications, there is still no clear understanding of what green logistics is, what the scope of application of this term is, and to what extent green logistics is integrated into logistics activities. The aim of this article is to provide a comprehensive review of scientific literature related to the concept of green logistics. This is to understand the essence of the term “Green logistics,” its evolution in the works of scientists around the world, and its integration into logistics activities. It also focuses on the concept of sustainable development. A set of methods, including the PRISMA methodology and content analysis of scientific publications from the Scopus database, was used in the study. We identified 56 original definitions of the term “Green logistics,” performed a meta-analysis of all definitions, and an analysis of the keywords most frequently used in the definitions. We also determined the evolution of the term under study and its connection with aspects of the concept of sustainable development. The results refine the concept and fields of use of the term “Green chain” and form the basis for further research into various types of logistics systems.
